body.description:
Find genes that are differentially expressed between two groups of samples in an RNA-Seq experiment. This search uses a guided notebook within ${projectName} that runs DESeq2, a widely-used statistical method for RNA-Seq differential expression analysis (Love et al., 2014).

How to run this search: Open the Configure Search tab and work through the notebook steps in order:
  • Select Expression Data — Choose the gene identifier variable and count type for the dataset.
  • Explore Sample Variation (optional) — Run a PCA to visualise sources of variation across samples. Use it to spot outliers or batch effects and exclude them before the DESeq2 step.
  • Define Sample Groups — Select a metadata variable (e.g. treatment, tissue type, or developmental stage) and assign samples to a Reference group and a Comparison group.
  • Set Thresholds — Explore the results on an interactive volcano plot. Adjust the effect size and p-value thresholds to highlight the genes you want to retrieve.
  • Run the Search — Click Get Answer to retrieve all genes that meet your criteria.

Effect size: The effect size is expressed as a log2 fold change — how much more or less a gene is expressed in the Comparison group relative to the Reference group. A positive value indicates up-regulation; a negative value indicates down-regulation.

P-value: DESeq2 computes both a raw p-value and a Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value for each gene. The volcano plot is drawn using the raw p-value (on a −log10 scale), and the p-value threshold you set on the plot is also applied to the raw p-value. Adjusted p-values are available in the mouse-over tooltip for each point on the volcano plot. A lower p-value (raw or adjusted) indicates a more statistically confident call.

Removing outliers: If the PCA plot reveals samples that cluster away from the rest (potential outliers or contaminated libraries), you can exclude them using the Select Samples step at the top of the notebook. Apply a filter on the sample identifier or a metadata variable to remove those samples before running DESeq2. Note that changing the sample subset will reset any group assignments you have already made in the DESeq2 step, so it is best to check the PCA first before defining your groups.

body.displayName: Protein targets of serum antibodies in response to infection Antibody Array
body.description:
Find proteins with differential abundance between two groups of samples in an antibody array experiment. This search uses a guided notebook within the site that runs Limma, a widely-used statistical method for analysing microarray and antibody array data (Ritchie et al., 2015).

How to run this search: Open the Configure Search tab and work through the notebook steps in order:
  • Select Antibody Array Data — Choose the antibody identifier variable and the signal type (measurement type) for the dataset.
  • Explore Sample Variation (optional) — Run a PCA to visualise sources of variation across samples. Use it to spot outliers or batch effects and exclude them before the Limma step.
  • Define Sample Groups — Select a metadata variable (e.g. treatment, tissue type, or disease status) and assign samples to a Reference group and a Comparison group.
  • Set Thresholds — Explore the results on an interactive volcano plot. Adjust the effect size and p-value thresholds to highlight the proteins you want to retrieve.
  • Run the Search — Click Get Answer to retrieve all proteins that meet your criteria.

Effect size: The effect size is expressed as a log2 fold change — how much more or less abundant a protein is in the Comparison group relative to the Reference group. A positive value indicates higher abundance in the Comparison group; a negative value indicates lower abundance.

P-value: Limma computes both a raw p-value and a Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value for each protein. The volcano plot is drawn using the raw p-value (on a −log10 scale), and the p-value threshold you set on the plot is also applied to the raw p-value. Adjusted p-values are available in the mouse-over tooltip for each point on the volcano plot. A lower p-value (raw or adjusted) indicates a more statistically confident call.

Removing outliers: If the PCA plot reveals samples that cluster away from the rest (potential outliers or contaminated arrays), you can exclude them using the Select Samples step at the top of the notebook. Apply a filter on the sample identifier or a metadata variable to remove those samples before running Limma. Note that changing the sample subset will reset any group assignments you have already made in the Limma step, so it is best to check the PCA first before defining your groups.

body.displayName: P. falciparum 3D7 Dual transcriptomes of malaria-infected Gambian children (RNA-Seq) WGCNA modules (functional prediction)
body.description:
Run this search: This search returns genes that belong to a specific WGCNA module. Choose your module of interest from the dropdown menu for the WGCNA Module parameter. (See the study explorer section below for tools on identifying a module that may be of interest to you.) Then choose the correlation coefficient that a gene's expression profile must share with the eigengene for the gene to be considered a member of the module. Click Get Answer to retrieve genes that meet your criteria.

WGCNA module: Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) identifies groups of genes that have similar expression across samples. The analysis considers the whole transcriptome data set and clusters co-expressed genes into groups called modules. The modules in VEuPathDB were found using an iterative Weighted Gene Correlation Network Analysis.

Eigengene: The eigengene is created in the WGCNA analysis and is an imaginary gene whose expression profile represents an average gene within the module. Each module is represented by an eigengene. It is very likely that no gene within the module has the same expression profile as the eigengene.

Study Explorer: Relationships between modules or between modules and study variables such as participant disease status (asymptomatic vs severe), blood parasitemia, or age, may reveal central players in biological processes associated with the whole transcriptome data set. Use the Study Explorer to browse variable distributions, analyze/visualize correlations between modules, and analyze/visualize correlations between modules and study variables.
body.searchVisibleHelp:
Study Explorer

Use the Study Explorer to discover WGCNA modules (co-expression networks) of interest. For example, a module may have a positive correlation with study metadata such as patient platelet count or age. The Study Explorer offers metadata filters and visualization tools to help conceptualize modules in relation to study variables so that you may discover and choose a module of interest.
